aciklama:
A dam holds back millions of tons of water - and it only takes one weak spot to unleash it all. Here is how dams fail.

#shorts #engineering #science #disaster #howitworks

sahneler.metin: A dam is one wall holding back an entire lake.
If it breaks, the water races downstream faster than a car.
The quiet killer is water seeping through it.
It slowly carries away soil, carving a hidden tunnel inside.
Engineers call this piping, and you cannot see it happening.
Once a small breach opens, the pressure rips it wide open.
Water pouring over the top erodes a dam in minutes.
That is why dams are monitored around the clock.

vaka.ders: dams are monitored with sensors around the clock
vaka.yanilgi: Dams rarely fail by cracking like glass. Overtopping and internal erosion — water slowly carving through the fill — are among the most common causes.
vaka.tartisma: Teton Dam failed in 1976 during its very first filling. Should new dams be filled more slowly?
